descriptionChirho: The Feast of Unleavened Bread (ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν ἀζύμων) or the literal unleavened bread eaten during Passover week; appears in the synoptic Passion narratives (Matthew 26:17, Mark 14:1, 14:12, Luke 22:1, 22:7) and in Paul's Passover metaphor context (1 Corinthians 5:8). Spanish panes-sin-levadura/ázimos, Arabic فَطيرِ/الْفَطِيرِ (fatir, the standard Arabic term for unleavened bread), Korean 무교병/무교절 (mugyobyeong 'unleavened bread'/mugyojeol 'unleavened-bread feast'), Hindi अखमीरी-रोटी ('unleavened bread'), Swahili mikate-isiyotiwa-chachu ('bread without yeast').

A metaphorical application of 'unleavened' to describe the morally purified state of believers who have removed the 'leaven' of sin and wickedness (1 Corinthians 5:7 'you are unleavened'); Paul commands the Corinthian church to be what they already are in Christ — pure and free from corruption. Spanish sin-levadura, Arabic فَطيرٌ (fatirun, predicative), Korean 누룩-없는-자들 ('people without leaven,' explicitly metaphorical), Hindi अखमीरी, Swahili bila-chachu ('without yeast'). The shift from neuter plural (the bread/feast) to masculine plural (the people) marks the figurative extension.
